text.tspan: BEYOND HUMAN SKIN
Beyond Human Skin
is an audiovisual project composed of moving image,
photography, and animation. The work emerged from a simple question:
what remains of the human if we stop imagining it as autonomous, closed,
and separated from the rest of the living world?
The project explores the body as a porous and multispecies ecosystem,
continuously shaped through coexistence with microorganisms,
environments, and other forms of life. Through moving image, photography,
illustration, and animation, the work investigates relationships between the
visible and invisible, the human and the more-than-human. Illustration
and animation become tools for imagining microscopic presences and
ecological entanglements that escape direct human perception.
The project originates from a desire to question anthropocentric
understandings of the body and rethink the human as part of a multispecies
ecology.
[link to the video: https://vimeo.com/1195950941?fl=pl&fe=sh ]
The project is informed by Lynn Margulis’ concept of the
*holobiont*, which understands the organism together with
its associated microbial communities as a multispecies
assemblage; Karen Barad’s notion of *intra-action*, through
which entities emerge relationally rather than existing
independently of their relations; and Donna Haraway’s
concept of *becoming-with*, which understands beings as
constituted through ongoing, situated relationships with
other species and forms of life. These ideas, together
with ecofeminist critiques of anthropocentrism and
hierarchical divisions between humans and the more-than-
human world, shaped my understanding of the human body as
relational, porous, and continuously co-constituted within
a multispecies world.
The project was developed through an intuitive and site-
responsive process in Sicily, a territory with which I have
a deeply personal connection. Rather than following a fixed
script, the work emerged through observation and intuitive
filming.
Audiovisual installation / moving image /
photography / animation. 2025
Presented at EContemporary Gallery during the
Trieste Film
Festival 2026
